<div id="A2.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">In the concrete setup, the total query numbers are set to <math id="A2.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q=8000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q=8000</annotation></semantics></math> for Metromap and <math id="A2.SS2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q=8400" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8400</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q=8400</annotation></semantics></math> for Travelmap.
The intra-group weighting exponent is fixed to <math id="A2.SS2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=1.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=1.5</annotation></semantics></math>, and the minimum query threshold is uniformly set to <math id="A2.SS2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q_{\min}=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q_{\min}=5</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">The significance of this algorithm lies in achieving fair and balanced query allocation across multi-city/multi-attraction and multi-difficulty experimental settings. It prevents large cities/attractions from monopolizing query resources while ensuring sufficient data support for smaller ones, strictly maintains training-test ratios, and preserves reasonable data distributions, thereby guaranteeing sufficient model training and reliable evaluation.
Moreover, the allocation results are traceable and controllable, ensuring that each city/attraction meets the minimum query threshold and providing a stable, interpretable, and reliable data foundation for multi-city/multi-attraction experiments.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.3 </span>Quality Control: Metromap Validation Algorithm</h3>

<div id="A2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This section introduces a Metromap-specific validation algorithm designed to ensure the accuracy and consistency of metro line data in Edge_tab and Vertex_tab.
The algorithm includes duplicate detection, station category comparison, vertex &amp; edge cross-validation, transfer station annotation verification, and manual inspection, comprehensively identifying potential annotation errors and data inconsistencies:</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ol id="A2.I2" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A2.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A2.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Duplicate detection:</span>
First, edges in Edge_tab and stations in Vertex_tab are checked for duplication within the same metro line (Line).
Specifically, if station A-B and B-A both appear, they are treated as the same edge. This step ensures the absence of redundant or duplicated metro information and verifies graph correctness.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A2.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Station category set comparison:</span>
Station categories in Edge_tab and Vertex_tab are collected and compared. This process checks for category consistency across the two files and helps identify annotation errors, especially when vertex and edge errors occur in different files.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="A2.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I2.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Vertex &amp; edge cross-validation:</span>
Based on the relationship between Edge_tab and Vertex_tab, the validation computes:
<math id="A2.I2.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\text{total number of edges in Edge\_tab})+(\text{number of metro line categories})-(\text{number of loop lines})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mtext>total number of edges in Edge_tab</mtext><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mtext>number of metro line categories</mtext><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mtext>number of loop lines</mtext><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\text{total number of edges in Edge\_tab})+(\text{number of metro line categories})-(\text{number of loop lines})</annotation></semantics></math>,
which should equal the total number of station occurrences in Vertex_tab.
Ordinary stations are counted once, while transfer stations are counted according to the number of lines they belong to.
This method detects cases where both Edge_tab and Vertex_tab contain errors that escape conventional validation.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I2.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="A2.I2.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I2.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I2.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Transfer station annotation verification:</span>
Transfer stations are checked separately in Edge_tab and Vertex_tab by expanding the set of lines each transfer station belongs to and comparing consistency across the two files.
Transfer station identification criteria are defined as follows:</p>
<ul id="A2.I2.i4.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A2.I2.i4.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I2.i4.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I2.i4.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I2.i4.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Edge_tab:</span> if the same station name appears on multiple metro lines.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I2.i4.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I2.i4.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I2.i4.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I2.i4.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Vertex_tab:</span> if a station’s Line column contains multiple lines or the Transfer Time value is greater than zero.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I2.i4.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I2.i4.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I2.i4.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I2.i4.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Loop line identification:</span> in Edge_tab, if the first and last stations of the same line are identical, the line is considered a loop line. This step ensures accurate transfer station annotation and avoids errors arising from loop line special cases.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I2.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">5.</span> 
<div id="A2.I2.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I2.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I2.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Manual verification:</span>
Finally, Edge_tab and Vertex_tab are manually checked against real metro maps to identify errors not detectable through automated validation.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.4 </span>Quality Control: Travelmap Validation Algorithm</h3>

<div id="A2.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Travelmap-specific validation algorithm retains steps 1, 2, and 5 from the Metromap validation algorithm, with appropriate modifications to step 2.
For Travelmap, Vertex_tab removes points that are completely disconnected from all others, retaining only connected vertices.
In addition, Edge_tab is required to contain a single fully connected graph, preventing the existence of multiple disconnected subgraphs.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Metrics</h2>

<div id="A3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This section proposes a unified evaluation framework designed to systematically assess model performance, map structural complexity, and query difficulty.</p>
</div>
<section id="A3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.1 </span>Performance Metrics</h3>

<div id="A3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For model performance evaluation, the RP task adopts three core metrics Exact Match Accuracy (EMA), Partial Match Accuracy (PMA), and Difficulty-aware Score (DS) to comprehensively measure model performance in terms of path correctness, linguistic consistency, and format compliance. Given that the output format is strictly constrained by prompts, any result that does not conform to the required format is regarded as incorrect. Such format generation failures themselves indicate deficiencies in the model’s instruction understanding and execution capabilities. For QA tasks, evaluation is conducted solely based on Accuracy (Acc).</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We first describe the performance metrics for the RP task in detail:</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">1. Exact Match Accuracy (EMA)</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">A score of 1 is assigned if the path generated by the model exactly matches the reference path in both station order and content; otherwise, a score of 0 is assigned. To tolerate minor spelling errors, a generated station name is considered identical to the reference station if the string similarity exceeds 50%. The similarity is computed based on character sequence matching, ignoring case differences and leading or trailing whitespaces. For Metromap, stations involving transfers must be explicitly annotated with the suffix “transfer”; otherwise, the station is considered incorrect. This transfer annotation requirement does not apply to Travelmap.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">2. Partial Match Accuracy (PMA)</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">PMA measures the length of the longest contiguous correct prefix in the generated path, starting from the origin. Evaluation is conducted at the station level, counting only the continuously matched prefix until the first mismatched station appears (excluding the mismatched station). The PMA score is computed as the ratio of the length of this correct prefix to the total length of the reference path. This metric is preferred over simply measuring the proportion of correctly repeated stations, as we assume that once an error occurs in the path, subsequent planning steps become invalid and no longer reflect meaningful routing decisions.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">3. Difficulty-aware Score (DS)</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p8.1" class="ltx_p">DS explicitly incorporates task difficulty into the evaluation. Each sample is assigned a discrete score ranging from 2 to 6 based on the combination of its Map_difficulty and Query_difficulty, denoted as Map_difficulty-Query_difficulty. Specifically, Easy, Medium, and Hard correspond to scores of 1, 2, and 3, respectively, and the final difficulty score is obtained by summing the two values. The difficulty score is counted only when EMA equals 1. This metric effectively reflects the upper bound of model performance, particularly its capability in handling high-difficulty tasks.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p9.1" class="ltx_p">For QA-query tasks, all questions are either binary (true/false) or fill-in-the-blank. Evaluation is conducted using Accuracy (Acc): a score of 1 is assigned if the model-generated answer exactly matches the reference answer; otherwise, a score of 0 is assigned.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.2 </span>Difficulty Classification Metrics</h3>

<div id="A3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This section introduces the classification methods for Map Difficulty and Query Difficulty. The core idea is to sort each Map and Query based on defined evaluation metrics and divide them into three levels: Hard, Medium, and Easy, with a ratio of 1:1:1. In Map Difficulty Classification, three indicators are considered: Graph Size (GS), Weighted Average Shortest Path (WASP), and Meshedness Coefficient (MC). In Query Difficulty Classification, addressing the specific scenarios of Metromap and Travelmap, the Shortest Path Length Index (SPLI) and Simple Path Complexity Index (SPCI) are adopted as difficulty metrics, respectively. These metrics comprehensively evaluate the complexity of Maps and Queries in RP tasks.</p>
</div>
<section id="A3.SS2.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">C.2.1 </span>Map Difficulty Classification</h4>

<div id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">1. Graph Size (GS)</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Graph Size represents the overall “scale” of the graph, i.e., the sum of the number of nodes and edges:</p>
<table id="A3.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="GS=|V|+|E|" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">GS=|V|+|E|</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|V|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|V|</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the number of nodes in the graph, and <math id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|E|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|E|</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the number of edges. This formula indicates that the size of the graph is equal to the sum of all nodes and edges, used to measure the complexity or overall volume of the graph.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">2. Weighted Average Shortest Path (WASP)</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">WASP measures the average shortest path length between nodes in the graph, while considering the potential existence of multiple connected components. Let graph <math id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>G</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G</annotation></semantics></math> have <math id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> connected components <math id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{1},C_{2},\dots,C_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{1},C_{2},\dots,C_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>, where the number of nodes in each connected component is <math id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{i}=|C_{i}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{i}=|C_{i}|</annotation></semantics></math>, and the shortest path length between nodes is <math id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d(u,v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d(u,v)</annotation></semantics></math>. The unified expression is:</p>
<table id="A3.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="WASP=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{k}|C_{i}|\cdot\text{ASPD}(C_{i})}{\sum_{i=1}^{k}|C_{i}|}=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{k}|C_{i}|\cdot\text{ASPD}(C_{i})}{|V|}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>W</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>k</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mtext>ASPD</mtext></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>k</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>k</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mtext>ASPD</mtext></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">WASP=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{k}|C_{i}|\cdot\text{ASPD}(C_{i})}{\sum_{i=1}^{k}|C_{i}|}=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{k}|C_{i}|\cdot\text{ASPD}(C_{i})}{|V|}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p4.2" class="ltx_p">Here, the inner summation and <math id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{ASPD}(C_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>ASPD</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{ASPD}(C_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> are used to calculate the average shortest path length of node pairs within each connected component; the outer summation sums these weighted by the number of nodes. When the graph is connected (<math id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=1</annotation></semantics></math>), WASP is equivalent to the ordinary average shortest path length.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">3. Meshedness Coefficient (MC)</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Meshedness Coefficient measures the degree of density (tightness) between nodes in the graph, usually defined by the relationship between the number of edges and the number of cycles:</p>
<table id="A3.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="MC=\frac{|E|-|V|+2}{|E|}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">MC=\frac{|E|-|V|+2}{|E|}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p6.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|V|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|V|</annotation></semantics></math> represents the number of nodes, and <math id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|E|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|E|</annotation></semantics></math> represents the number of edges. When <math id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|E|&gt;|V|-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|E|&gt;|V|-1</annotation></semantics></math>, cycles exist in the graph, and a larger Mesh Coefficient (MC) indicates more cycles in the graph and tighter connections between nodes.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">For Metromap, each sample considers only two metrics: Graph Size (GS) and Weighted Average Shortest Path (WASP). Each indicator was first normalized and subsequently aggregated by computing their arithmetic mean. Samples are sorted by this average value and strictly divided into three levels: Hard, Medium, and Easy, with a ratio of 1:1:1.
For Travelmap, the GS, WASP, and MC metrics are considered simultaneously. To ensure a balanced distribution of Map Difficulty levels in both the training and test sets, the algorithm groups every three consecutive samples after sorting. From each group, one sample is randomly selected for the test set, and the other two for the training set, thereby balancing the train/test ratio and difficulty levels.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS2.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">C.2.2 </span>Query Difficulty Classification</h4>

<div id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In RP tasks, the structural characteristics of Metromap and Travelmap differ significantly: the former has many intersection points and an extremely large number of simple paths between nodes, making the calculation of the average length of all simple paths overly complex, so it is only suitable to use the Shortest Path Length Index (SPLI) for measurement. The latter has a relatively small number of simple paths, so using the Simple Path Complexity Index (SPCI) to calculate the average length of all simple paths can more objectively reflect RP difficulty.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">1. Shortest Path Length Index (SPLI)</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">SPLI measures the shortest path length from source point <math id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> to target point <math id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> in the graph, i.e., the number of edges passed by the shortest path between points. This metric is used to evaluate the connection efficiency between nodes. For Metromap, which has many intersections and a massive number of simple paths, using only the shortest path length can effectively characterize query difficulty:</p>
<table id="A3.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="SPLI(s,t)=\min(L_{1},L_{2},\dots,L_{n})" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">SPLI(s,t)=\min(L_{1},L_{2},\dots,L_{n})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p3.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> represents the length of all paths from <math id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> in the graph.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">2. Simple Path Complexity Index (SPCI)</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">SPCI measures the average length of all simple paths (paths without repeating nodes) from source point <math id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> to target point <math id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> in the graph, used to characterize path complexity. A higher SPCI value indicates more selectable paths and a more complex structure. For Travelmap, it can objectively reflect the diversified connections and query difficulty between source and target points:</p>
<table id="A3.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="SPCI(s,t)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}l(L_{i})" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></munderover><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">SPCI(s,t)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}l(L_{i})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p5.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> is the number of all simple paths from <math id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l(L_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l(L_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> is the length of path <math id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p6.1" class="ltx_p">The number of queries per image is determined by the algorithm described in Appendix <a href="#A2.SS2" title="B.2 RP Query Distribution Based on Difficulty Classification Metrics ‣ Appendix B More Details for Dataset Construction ‣ MapTab: Can MLLMs Master Constrained Route Planning?" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.2</span></a>. Subsequently, after query generation, Query Difficulty Classification is performed for each image. In Metromap and Travelmap, queries are sorted according to their respective difficulty metrics and strictly divided into Hard, Medium, and Easy levels in equal proportions.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Query Template</h2>

<section id="A4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.1 </span>RP Query</h3>

<div id="A4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this study, we design a series of RP queries based on <span id="A4.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Metromap</span> and <span id="A4.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Travelmap</span> to evaluate path optimization algorithms under different input modalities and constraint settings. Taking the <span id="A4.SS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Map-Only</span> setting in <span id="A4.SS1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Metromap</span> as an example, where {station_1} and {station_2} denote randomly sampled origin-destination pairs described in Section <a href="#S3.SS3.SSS1" title="3.3.1 Question Generation ‣ 3.3 Queries Construction ‣ 3 MapTab Building Pipeline ‣ MapTab: Can MLLMs Master Constrained Route Planning?" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3.1</span></a>, we formulate five types of queries with different instruction styles as follows:</p>
<ol id="A4.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A4.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A4.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Direct Optimization query</span>: According to the Subway Map, what is the path with the fewest stations from {station_1} to {station_2}?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A4.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Graph-theoretic</span>: According to the Subway Map, what is the shortest path from {station_1} to {station_2}?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="A4.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Instruction-seeking</span>: According to the Subway Map, how can I reach {station_2} from {station_1} via the shortest path?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="A4.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">User-oriented Optimization</span>: According to the Subway Map, how can I travel from {station_1} to {station_2} with the fewest number of stations?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">5.</span> 
<div id="A4.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I1.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Constraint-explicit Optimization</span>: According to the Subway Map, what is the shortest route in terms of station count from {station_1} to {station_2}?</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">All remaining queries are also constructed with these five instruction styles. For brevity, we list only the <span id="A4.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Direct Optimization query</span> style below:</p>
<ul id="A4.I2" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A4.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A4.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Unconstrained - Edge_tab-Only</span>: According to Edge Table and Vertex Table, what is the path with the fewest stations from {station_1} to {station_2}?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A4.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Unconstrained - Map+Edge_tab</span>: According to the Subway Map, Edge Table and Vertex Table, what is the path with the fewest stations from {station_1} to {station_2}?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A4.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I2.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Single/Multi-constraint - Map+Edge_tab+Vertex_tab</span>:</p>
<ol id="A4.I2.i3.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Time-Only</span>: According to the Subway Map, Edge Table and Vertex Table, what is the fastest route from {station_1} to {station_2}?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Price-Only</span>: According to the Subway Map, Edge Table and Vertex Table, what is the cheapest route from {station_1} to {station_2}?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Comfort Level-Only</span>: According to the Subway Map, Edge Table and Vertex Table, what is the smoothest ride between {station_1} and {station_2}?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Reliability-Only</span>: According to the Subway Map, Edge Table and Vertex Table, what is the most stable subway route from {station_1} to {station_2}?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">5.</span> 
<div id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Time+Price+Reliability</span>: According to the Subway Map, Edge Table and Vertex Table, what is the optimal route considering time, price, and reliability from {station_1} to {station_2}?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">6.</span> 
<div id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Time+Comfort Level+Reliability</span>: According to the Subway Map, Edge Table and Vertex Table, what is the fastest, most comfortable, and reliable route from {station_1} to {station_2}?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i7" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">7.</span> 
<div id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Price+Comfort Level+Reliability</span>: According to the Subway Map, Edge Table and Vertex Table, what is the best route optimizing price, comfort, and reliability from {station_1} to {station_2}?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i8" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">8.</span> 
<div id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i8.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I2.i3.I0.i8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Time+Price+Comfort Level+Reliability</span>: According to the Subway Map, Edge Table and Vertex Table, what is the optimal route considering time, price, comfort, and reliability from {station_1} to {station_2}?</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I2.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A4.I2.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I2.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I2.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Multi-constraint - Map+Vertex_tab</span>: According to the Subway Map and the Vertex Table, what is the optimal route considering time, price, comfort, and reliability from {station_1} to {station_2}?</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">For <span id="A4.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Travelmap</span>, the term “Subway Map” is replaced with “Scenic Area Planning Map” in all queries.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.2 </span>QA Query</h3>

<div id="A4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In addition to RP queries, we design a series of QA queries based on <span id="A4.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Metromap</span> and <span id="A4.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Travelmap</span>. The experimental setup systematically considers four input modalities: <span id="A4.SS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Map-Only</span>, <span id="A4.SS2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Edge_tab-Only</span>, <span id="A4.SS2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Vertex_tab-Only</span>, and <span id="A4.SS2.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Map+Vertex_tab</span>. For <span id="A4.SS2.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Metromap</span>, the <span id="A4.SS2.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Vertex_tab</span> excludes the <span id="A4.SS2.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Line</span> column, enabling an explicit evaluation of multimodal joint reasoning under missing single-modality information.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Under each modality, we construct three categories of tasks: <span id="A4.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Global Perception-based Reasoning Tasks (GP)</span>, <span id="A4.SS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Local Perception-based Reasoning Tasks (LP)</span>, and <span id="A4.SS2.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Spatial Relationship Judgment Tasks (SR)</span>. Each QA category is instantiated with five semantically equivalent but stylistically distinct instruction templates, including <span id="A4.SS2.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Direct / Neutral</span>, <span id="A4.SS2.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Simple &amp; Conversational</span>, <span id="A4.SS2.p2.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Slightly Formal</span>, <span id="A4.SS2.p2.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Technical / Academic Style</span>, and <span id="A4.SS2.p2.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Concise / Dataset-Friendly</span>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Taking the <span id="A4.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Map-Only</span> <span id="A4.SS2.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Global Perception-based Reasoning Tasks (GP)</span> as an example, the five instruction styles are as follows:</p>
<ol id="A4.I3" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A4.I3.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A4.I3.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I3.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I3.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Direct / Neutral</span>: How many metro lines are there in total on the Subway Map?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I3.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A4.I3.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I3.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I3.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Simple &amp; Conversational</span>: How many subway lines are shown on the metro map?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I3.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="A4.I3.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I3.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I3.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Slightly Formal</span>: What is the total number of rail lines in the Subway Map?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I3.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="A4.I3.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I3.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I3.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Technical / Academic Style</span>: How many distinct transit lines does the metro map contain?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I3.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">5.</span> 
<div id="A4.I3.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I3.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I3.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Concise / Dataset-Friendly</span>: What is the total count of metro lines in the map?</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">All QA tasks follow the same five-style formulation. Below, we list a subset of queries using only the <span id="A4.SS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Direct / Neutral</span> style:</p>
<ol id="A4.I4" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A4.I4.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A4.I4.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I4.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Metromap-Map - GP: How many metro lines are there in total on the Subway Map?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I4.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A4.I4.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I4.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Metromap-Map - LP: How many stations are there between {Station A} and {Station B} on the same line?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I4.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="A4.I4.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I4.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Metromap-Map - SR: Is {Station A} on Line X?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I4.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="A4.I4.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I4.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Metromap-Edge_tab - GP: What is the number of stations on the longest subway line?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I4.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">5.</span> 
<div id="A4.I4.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I4.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Metromap-Edge_tab - LP: What is the Time/Price/Comfort Level value for the edge {Station A}-{Station B}?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I4.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">6.</span> 
<div id="A4.I4.i6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I4.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Metromap-Edge_tab - SR: How many edges are there between the edge {Station A}-{Station B} and the edge {Station C}-{Station D}?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I4.i7" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">7.</span> 
<div id="A4.I4.i7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I4.i7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Metromap-Vertex_tab - GP: How many transfer stations are there in the entire table?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I4.i8" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">8.</span> 
<div id="A4.I4.i8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I4.i8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Metromap-Vertex_tab - LP: How many transfer stations are there on {Line X}?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I4.i9" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">9.</span> 
<div id="A4.I4.i9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I4.i9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Metromap-Vertex_tab - SR: Are {Station A} and {Station B} on the same line?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I4.i10" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">10.</span> 
<div id="A4.I4.i10.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I4.i10.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Metromap-Map+Vertex_tab - GP: What is the total stop time of the subway line with the longest stop time?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I4.i11" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">11.</span> 
<div id="A4.I4.i11.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I4.i11.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Metromap-Map+Vertex_tab - LP: What is the average reliability from {Station A} to {Station B} on the same line?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I4.i12" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">12.</span> 
<div id="A4.I4.i12.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I4.i12.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Metromap-Map+Vertex_tab - SR: Please check if there are transfer stations between {Line X} and {Line Y}. If there are, return the shortest transfer time; if not, return 0. If there is only one subway line, return 1.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I4.i13" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">13.</span> 
<div id="A4.I4.i13.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I4.i13.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Travelmap-Map - GP: How many tourist attractions are there in total?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I4.i14" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">14.</span> 
<div id="A4.I4.i14.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I4.i14.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Travelmap-Map - LP: Is scenic {Spot A} on the circular route?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I4.i15" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">15.</span> 
<div id="A4.I4.i15.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I4.i15.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Travelmap-Map - SR: How many scenic spots are adjacent to scenic {Spot A}?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I4.i16" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">16.</span> 
<div id="A4.I4.i16.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I4.i16.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Travelmap-Edge_tab - GP: How many times does the most frequently appearing scenic spot appear in the table?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I4.i17" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">17.</span> 
<div id="A4.I4.i17.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I4.i17.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Travelmap-Edge_tab - LP: What is the value of Time/Price for {Spot A}-{Spot B}?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I4.i18" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">18.</span> 
<div id="A4.I4.i18.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I4.i18.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Travelmap-Edge_tab - SR: Is the shortest distance between {Spot A} and {Spot B} less than 5?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I4.i19" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">19.</span> 
<div id="A4.I4.i19.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I4.i19.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Travelmap-Vertex_tab - GP: How many scenic spots in the table have a Time value less than 30?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I4.i20" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">20.</span> 
<div id="A4.I4.i20.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I4.i20.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Travelmap-Vertex_tab - LP: Given {Spot A}, {Spot B}, {Spot C}, and {Spot D}, what is the price of the cheapest one?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I4.i21" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">21.</span> 
<div id="A4.I4.i21.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I4.i21.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Travelmap-Vertex_tab - SR: Is {Spot A} located above {Spot B} in the table?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I4.i22" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">22.</span> 
<div id="A4.I4.i22.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I4.i22.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Travelmap-Map+Vertex_tab - GP: Is the number of scenic spots in the table the same as the actual number of scenic spots in the map?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I4.i23" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">23.</span> 
<div id="A4.I4.i23.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I4.i23.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Travelmap-Map+Vertex_tab - LP: Are there any locations with Time <math id="A4.I4.i23.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&lt;" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>&lt;</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&lt;</annotation></semantics></math> 30 along all shortest paths from {Spot A} to {Spot B}?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I4.i24" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">24.</span> 
<div id="A4.I4.i24.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I4.i24.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Travelmap-Map+Vertex_tab - SR: What is the cost of the lowest-priced location adjacent to {Spot A}?</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">The design of this task suite ensures that the QA queries can effectively reveal the intrinsic characteristics of the dataset, thereby providing support for better training framework design in subsequent RP tasks. Moreover, the tasks span diverse modalities and reasoning challenges, offering rich instruction styles and task scenarios to comprehensively evaluate model performance.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Prompt Template</h2>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this study, the prompt templates are divided into two categories: one for RP tasks and the other for QA tasks. Since the prompt construction methods for <span id="A5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Metromap</span> and <span id="A5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Travelmap</span> are identical, we take the prompts for <span id="A5.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Metromap</span> as an illustrative example below.</p>
</div>
<section id="A5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.1 </span>Prompts for Generating Edge_tab and Vertex_tab</h3>

<div id="A5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this work, we design the <span id="A5.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Edge_tab</span> and <span id="A5.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Vertex_tab</span> attributes for <span id="A5.SS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Metromap</span> and <span id="A5.SS1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Travelmap</span> based on real-world transportation networks and connectivity characteristics between metro systems and scenic areas. Specifically, the attributes in <span id="A5.SS1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Edge_tab</span> capture key operational characteristics of metro systems and scenic routes, including time, price, comfort level, and reliability, which are used to simulate the operational properties of different paths and the corresponding user experience. In contrast, the attributes in <span id="A5.SS1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Vertex_tab</span> focus on the characteristics of metro stations and scenic spots, covering dwell time, comfort level, price, reliability, and transfer time, thereby modeling the transfer complexity between stations or attractions as well as the passenger experience at each location. Through the design of these attributes, we aim to faithfully reflect the diverse factors that must be considered in RP tasks, ensuring the scientific validity and rationality of model behavior during path selection and optimization. The specific attribute designs and their underlying rationales are described below.</p>
</div>
<section id="A5.SS1.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">E.1.1 </span>Metromap-Edge_tab</h4>

<div id="A5.SS1.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Based on real-world characteristics between adjacent metro stations, we design the attributes in the <span id="A5.SS1.SSS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Metromap Edge_tab</span> as follows:</p>
<ol id="A5.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A5.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A5.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Line</span>: This attribute indicates the metro line to which a station belongs, represented in the form of <span id="A5.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">x Line</span>, where <span id="A5.I1.i1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">x</span> denotes the line number or name.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.I1.i1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I1.i1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I1.i1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Design Rationale</span>: This attribute is used solely to annotate the metro line associated with each segment, facilitating the distinction between different lines and clarifying the connectivity relationships between stations.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A5.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A5.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Time</span>: This attribute simulates the travel time between Station A and Station B, with values ranging from 2.00 to 3.00 minutes, rounded to two decimal places.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.I1.i2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I1.i2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I1.i2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Design Rationale</span>: This range reflects typical travel durations between adjacent stations in urban metro systems.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A5.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="A5.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Price</span>: This attribute takes values ranging from 0.00 to 1.50 RMB, rounded to two decimal places.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.I1.i3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I1.i3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I1.i3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Design Rationale</span>: This range is intended to simulate a broad spectrum of metro fare levels, which commonly fluctuate within this interval across many cities.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A5.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="A5.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Comfort Level</span>: This attribute models passengers’ perceived comfort, with values ranging from 0.00 to 1.00, rounded to two decimal places.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.I1.i4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I1.i4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I1.i4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Design Rationale</span>: The range from 0.00 to 1.00 represents a spectrum from extremely poor to excellent riding experiences. Considering that real-world metro comfort may be affected by factors such as carriage crowding, air quality, and noise, this range reasonably captures variations in passenger comfort perception.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A5.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">5.</span> 
<div id="A5.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I1.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Reliability</span>: This attribute is set to 0.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.I1.i5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I1.i5.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I1.i5.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Design Rationale</span>: Since metro services would not operate if they were unreliable, all routes in this model are assumed to be reliable by default, and reliability is therefore not explicitly differentiated.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS1.SSS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.SSS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The generation prompt for <span id="A5.SS1.SSS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Edge_tab</span> in <span id="A5.SS1.SSS1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Metromap</span> as implemented in the Gemini-3-Flash model is specified as follows:</p>
<div id="A5.SS1.SSS1.p2.2" class="ltx_listing ltx_lstlisting ltx_listing"><div class="ltx_listing_data"><a href="data:text/plain;base64," download="">⬇</a></div>
<div id="lstnumberx1" class="ltx_listingline">#<span id="lstnumberx1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">Role</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx2" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">You</span><span id="lstnumberx2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">are</span><span id="lstnumberx2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx2.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">a</span><span id="lstnumberx2.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>**<span id="lstnumberx2.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">table</span>-<span id="lstnumberx2.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">generation</span><span id="lstnumberx2.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx2.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">agent</span>**<span id="lstnumberx2.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx2.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">that</span><span id="lstnumberx2.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx2.14" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">generates</span><span id="lstnumberx2.15" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx2.16" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">metro</span><span id="lstnumberx2.17" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx2.18" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">edge</span><span id="lstnumberx2.19" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx2.20" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">data</span>.
</div>

<section id="A5.SS1.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">E.1.2 </span>Metromap-Vertex_tab</h4>

<div id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Based on real-world characteristics of metro stations, we design the attributes in the <span id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Metromap Vertex_tab</span> as follows:</p>
<ol id="A5.I2" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A5.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A5.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Line</span>: This attribute indicates the metro line to which a station belongs, represented in the form of <span id="A5.I2.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">x Line</span>, where <span id="A5.I2.i1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">x</span> denotes the line number or name.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.I2.i1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I2.i1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I2.i1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Design Rationale</span>: This attribute is used to annotate the line associated with each metro station, enabling the model to distinguish stations belonging to different lines.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A5.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A5.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Time</span>: This attribute simulates the dwell time at each metro station, with values ranging from 0.50 to 2.00 minutes, rounded to two decimal places.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.I2.i2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I2.i2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I2.i2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Design Rationale</span>: This attribute models the time a train stops at a station, with values determined by simulated passenger flow and station-specific characteristics.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A5.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="A5.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I2.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Price</span>: This attribute is set to 0.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.I2.i3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I2.i3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I2.i3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Design Rationale</span>: Since no additional cost is incurred during station dwell time, pricing is only considered during metro travel segments.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A5.I2.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="A5.I2.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I2.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I2.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Comfort Level</span>: This attribute models passengers’ perceived comfort, with values ranging from 0.00 to 1.00, rounded to two decimal places.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.I2.i4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I2.i4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I2.i4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Design Rationale</span>: The range from 0.00 to 1.00 is designed to simulate variations in boarding and alighting volumes as well as station crowding levels.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A5.I2.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">5.</span> 
<div id="A5.I2.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I2.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I2.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Reliability</span>: This attribute takes values ranging from 0.50 to 1.00, rounded to two decimal places.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.I2.i5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I2.i5.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I2.i5.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Design Rationale</span>: This range simulates the probability of station disruptions and downtime caused by unexpected events (e.g., security incidents or equipment failures), reflecting reliability differences across stations.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A5.I2.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">6.</span> 
<div id="A5.I2.i6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I2.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I2.i6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Transfer Time</span>: This attribute represents the time required for transfers, with values ranging from 5 to 15 minutes, specified as integers.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.I2.i6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I2.i6.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I2.i6.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Design Rationale</span>: This range reflects the time cost of transfers between stations, varying according to transfer complexity and the physical distance between metro lines.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The generation prompt for <span id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Vertex_tab</span> in <span id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Metromap</span> as implemented in the Gemini-3-Flash model is specified as follows:</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<div id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p3.1" class="ltx_listing ltx_lstlisting ltx_listing"><div class="ltx_listing_data"><a href="data:text/plain;base64," download="">⬇</a></div>

</div>
<div id="lstnumberx36" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx36.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">You</span><span id="lstnumberx36.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx36.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">are</span><span id="lstnumberx36.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx36.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">a</span><span id="lstnumberx36.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>**<span id="lstnumberx36.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">table</span>-<span id="lstnumberx36.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">generation</span><span id="lstnumberx36.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx36.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">agent</span>**<span id="lstnumberx36.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx36.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">that</span><span id="lstnumberx36.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx36.14" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">generates</span><span id="lstnumberx36.15" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx36.16" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">metro</span><span id="lstnumberx36.17" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>**<span id="lstnumberx36.18" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">Vertex</span>**<span id="lstnumberx36.19" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx36.20" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">data</span>.

<div id="lstnumberx37" class="ltx_listingline">
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx38" class="ltx_listingline">#<span id="lstnumberx38.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx38.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">Rules</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx39" class="ltx_listingline">-<span id="lstnumberx39.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>**<span id="lstnumberx39.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">Strictly</span><span id="lstnumberx39.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx39.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">generate</span><span id="lstnumberx39.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx39.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">a</span><span id="lstnumberx39.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx39.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">metro</span><span id="lstnumberx39.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx39.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">Vertex</span><span id="lstnumberx39.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx39.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">table</span><span id="lstnumberx39.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx39.14" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">only</span>.**

<div id="lstnumberx40" class="ltx_listingline">-<span id="lstnumberx40.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>**<span id="lstnumberx40.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">Output</span><span <section id="A5.SS1.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">E.1.3 </span>Travelmap-Edge_tab</h4>

<div id="A5.SS1.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Based on real-world transportation networks and road connectivity characteristics between tourist attractions, we design the attributes in the <span id="A5.SS1.SSS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Travelmap Edge_tab</span> as follows:</p>
<ol id="A5.I3" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A5.I3.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A5.I3.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I3.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I3.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Time</span>: This attribute simulates the commuting time from one attraction to another. If the map explicitly provides a time annotation, that value is directly used. If only distance information is available and the distance exceeds 1 km, the time is computed assuming a speed of 60 km/h. If the distance is less than 1 km, a speed of 4 m/s is assumed and the resulting time is converted into minutes. Any computed time shorter than 1 minute is rounded up to 1 minute. If neither time nor distance information is provided, a random integer between 10 and 60 minutes is generated.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.I3.i1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I3.i1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I3.i1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Design Rationale</span>: Commuting time is inferred from the time or distance annotations provided on the map, or otherwise simulated using reasonable assumptions based on common transportation knowledge.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A5.I3.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A5.I3.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I3.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I3.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Price</span>: This attribute is a randomly generated integer ranging from 10 to 80, with smaller values occurring more frequently.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.I3.i2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I3.i2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I3.i2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Design Rationale</span>: This attribute simulates commuting costs, reflecting price variations across different routes or transportation modes. The biased random generation toward lower prices captures realistic cost distribution patterns observed in daily travel.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A5.I3.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="A5.I3.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I3.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I3.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Comfort Level</span>: This attribute models passengers’ perceived comfort using a travel-review-style rating scheme (e.g., from tourism applications such as Ctrip or Dianping). A single-decimal value is randomly generated within the range of 1.0 to 5.0, with ratings <math id="A5.I3.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\geq" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>≥</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\geq</annotation></semantics></math> 3.0 accounting for the majority.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.I3.i3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I3.i3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I3.i3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Design Rationale</span>: This attribute simulates comfort experiences across different routes or transportation modes, where higher comfort scores are typically associated with better vehicles, routes, or environmental conditions.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A5.I3.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="A5.I3.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I3.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I3.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Reliability</span>: This attribute is defined as <math id="A5.I3.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a/365" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>365</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a/365</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A5.I3.i4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> is an integer ranging from 1 to 365, with values greater than 180 occurring more frequently. The final value is reported with six decimal places.
<span id="A5.I3.i4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Design Rationale</span>: This attribute simulates route reliability by accounting for potential disruptions such as road construction, security controls, or closures of high-risk areas. Here, <math id="A5.I3.i4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> represents the number of days a route is effectively accessible within a year; larger values indicate higher reliability, reflecting lower frequencies of closures or access restrictions due to special events.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS1.SSS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.SSS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The generation prompt for <span id="A5.SS1.SSS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Edge_tab</span> in <span id="A5.SS1.SSS3.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Travelmap</span>, as implemented in the Gemini-3-Flash model, is specified as follows:</p>

</div>
<div id="lstnumberx73" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx73.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">You</span><span id="lstnumberx73.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span <div id="lstnumberx75" class="ltx_listingline">#<span id="lstnumberx75.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx75.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">Rules</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx76" class="ltx_listingline">-<span id="lstnumberx76.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>**<span id="lstnumberx76.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">Strictly</span><span id="lstnumberx76.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx76.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">generate</span><span id="lstnumberx76.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx76.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">an</span><span id="lstnumberx76.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx76.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">Edge</span><span id="lstnumberx76.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx76.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">table</span><span id="lstnumberx76.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx76.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">only</span>.**

<div id="lstnumberx77" class="ltx_listingline">-<span id="lstnumberx77.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>**<span id="lstnumberx77.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">Output</span><span
